source_findings.evidence: In s35 band0 and finalcrop-s35-0 the cue before ויכלו reads חו״ק, and both readers agree on it (comparison s35/vayekhulu_role). חו״ק stands for חזן וקהל. The expansion reverses the order. meein_sheva.xml correctly expands קו״ח as קהל וחזן.
source_findings.proposed_correction: <tei:expan>חזן וקהל</tei:expan>. Keep the shared corresp role/reader_and_congregation if the project accepts it for both orders.

source_findings.evidence: s38 band2 prints כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ, יְהוָה יִמְלֹךְ and וְנֶאֱמַר, וְהָיָה. The comma belongs to the citation formula, but in the XML it sits inside the semantic quotation span and inside the verse milestone scope. A transclusion of exodus/15/18 or zechariah/14/9 would therefore start with a comma.
source_findings.proposed_correction: Move each comma after the formula word and before the chapter/verse milestones: …בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ, <milestone chapter/><milestone verse/><seg>יְהוָה…</seg> and …וְנֶאֱמַר, <milestone …/><seg>וְהָיָה…</seg>.

guideline_findings.evidence: The whole canonical prayer:meein_sheva is gated on the Ten Days. The source prints a fixed הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and has no rubric or brackets. Any reuse of this canonical identity outside the Ten Days evaluates false and transcludes nothing. That over-claims a calendar condition for the entire text, when only one wording marks the witness as a Ten Days witness. The expanded edition already declares aseret-ymei-tshuva true, so the gate adds nothing there.
guideline_findings.proposed_correction: Remove the whole-file conditional and treat the file as a fixed Ten Days witness, as already done for the maḥzor Half Kaddish. If a condition is wanted, scope it to the המלך הקדוש wording only.

order_findings.exact_words: <tei:note type="description" xml:lang="en">At the meal, recite Hamotzi over the two loaves; taste the bread, then dip a piece of sweet apple in honey.</tei:note>
order_findings.evidence: This is invented English paraphrase, which the brief does not allow. It also puts the apple-dipping direction before the Hamotzi text, so it no longer introduces בורא פרי העץ, and it drops 'After Kiddush at the meal'. In the source (s36 band2), one instruction runs: 'After Kiddush at the meal, one recites המוציא over the two loaves. After tasting the bread, one dips a piece of sweet apple in honey and says:'.
order_findings.proposed_correction: Replace it with the verbatim source instruction (type=instruction, with tei:foreign for המוציא), placed before the Birnbaum Hamotzi. Alternatively, place only its second sentence immediately before borei_peri_haetz. Do not write new English.

order_findings.exact_words: <tei:note type="description" xml:lang="en">Bameh Madlikin: on Shabbat; the printed Frankfurt custom also includes it as on Shabbat.</tei:note>
order_findings.evidence: This is invented English. Because it is a description, it is also printed on every true evaluation, including an ordinary Shabbat. The source's own German rubric 'אין פֿראַנקפֿורט אַם מאַין בעטעט מאַן במה מדליקין וויא אַם שבת.' is dropped from the expanded edition, so its condition loses the printed wording.
order_findings.proposed_correction: Remove the English note. Put the source German rubric (xml:lang de-Hebr) as the conditional's tei:note type=instruction, so it prints only while the condition is undecided. The j:all wrapping a single j:any is redundant and may be simplified.

order_findings.evidence: These are reader-facing 'when' conditions inside a service, not running-order gates. When Shabbat is undecided (no date is declared), Vayekhulu, Meein Sheva and the home Vayekhulu print with no rubric or delimiters. The source supplies 'אַם שַׁבָּת:' (s35) and 'but on the Sabbath preceded by ויכלו' (s36). HE kiddush_vayekhulu.xml carries no note of its own, while the EN file does.
order_findings.proposed_correction: Add the source rubric 'אַם שַׁבָּת:' (de-Hebr) as the conditional note for the synagogue Vayekhulu/Meein Sheva. For the home Vayekhulu, either rely on a verbatim copy of the s36 'At home too…' instruction or reuse 'אַם שַׁבָּת:'. Do not invent a new note.
